--- cssclasses: - wide tags: - notes --- # What is Docker? docker is an app that makes migrating systems, servers, databases, etc. a lot easier. the way docker does it is with **images** and **containers**. just let the next machine **install docker only**, and it's ready to migrate! # What if we don't use docker? if you don't use docker when migrating, the system might break. it could be because of: - outdated / unstable software, - no prerequisite packages, - inconsistent configuration, - and more. # Images images are one of the key features of docker. images are packages that are ready to be copied and deployed to your container so it can be used immediately. > [!note] Analogy > think of an image as a photo of a document. you can still read the document right? but you can't edit it, just scan it. > once the image has been scanned, it can then be edited again and be used again. > > in plainer terms: the image is the frozen package — you don't touch it yourself. you **run** it, and what's running it is the container. one image can spawn as many copies of a container as you want. # Containers containers are also one of the key features of docker. containers are basically tiny virtual machines with their own apps and services running — and those services would be your running images. # Setting up docker ## Images needed - mysql - php ## Create network ```bash docker network create [name of network] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > docker network create webdev-network > ``` ## most basic command to create a container > [!danger] DISCLAIMER > **NOT RECOMMENDED TO RUN THIS BY ITSELF** ```bash docker run -d [name of container] ``` > [!warning] why it's not recommended > a bare `run` like this has no network, no volume, no environment variables, nothing. the full versions below include all of those — use those instead. ## command to find if a port is used (windows) ```bash netstat -ano | findstr [portnumber] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > netstat -ano | findstr 3306 > ``` > if something is using port `3306`, you get output like this. if the port is free, the command just prints nothing. > ``` > TCP 0.0.0.0:3306 0.0.0.0:0 LISTENING 18196 > TCP [::]:3306 [::]:0 LISTENING 18196 > ``` # Creating containers this is where containers actually get created. the templates here take the full `docker run` from earlier and add the network, volume, environment variables, and port mapping you'll actually need in class. ## MySQL container ```bash docker run -d --name [ContainerName] --network [NetworkName] -v [Volume Name]:[Volume Location] -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=[Mysql Password] -e MYSQL_DATABASE=[DatabaseName] -p [host port]:[container port] [image to be installed] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > docker run -d --name webdev-mysql --network webdev-network -v webdev-db-data:/var/lib/mysql -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root -e MYSQL_DATABASE=webdev-db -p 3310:3306 mysql:8.0 > ``` ## phpMyAdmin container ```bash docker run -d --name [ContainerName] --network [NetworkName] -e PMA_HOST=[MysqlContainerName] -p [host port]:[container port] [image to be installed] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > docker run -d --name webdev-phpmyadmin --network webdev-network -e PMA_HOST=webdev-mysql -p 3311:80 phpmyadmin > ``` ## My command > [!danger] DISCLAIMER > **DO NOT COPY THIS. THIS COMMAND IS IRRELEVANT TO YOUR PROJECTS** ```bash docker run -d --name EB_mysql --network EB_Network -v EB-db-data:/var/lib/mysql -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root -e MYSQL_DATABASE=EB_shop -p 6967:3306 mysql:8.0 ``` ```bash docker run -d --name EB_phpmyadmin --network EB_Network -e PMA_HOST=EB_mysql -p 6969:80 phpmyadmin ``` --- # Extra docker commands from the notes of Sir Ariel Bensing. ## Build an image from a dockerfile ```bash docker build -t symfony-app . ``` the `.` at the end matters — it points to the dockerfile in the **current folder**. ## Build the container based on the image ```bash docker run --name symfony-app-demo --network platform-network -p 8000:8000 symfony-app ``` ## Create a network ```bash docker network create platform-network ``` ## Build a container for MySQL ```bash docker run -d --name symfony-db --network platform-network -v symfony-db-data:/var/lib/mysql -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root -e MYSQL_DATABASE=app_db -p 3310:3306 mysql:8.0 ``` ## Build a container for phpMyAdmin ```bash docker run -d --name symfony-pma --network platform-network -p 8081:80 -e PMA_HOST=symfony-db phpmyadmin ``` ## Execute a command inside a running container ```bash docker exec -it symfony-app-demo "symfony command" ``` ## Inspect a network ```bash docker network inspect [network name] ``` ## Delete a network ```bash docker network rm [network name] ``` ## Delete a container ```bash docker rm [container name] ``` ## Delete an image ```bash docker rmi [image name] ``` ## Stop a container ```bash docker stop [container name] ``` took me a while to realize `stop` is for containers, not networks lmao. networks don't stop, they just exist until you `rm` them. --- # Extra on symfony to connect to your database you have to open your `.env` file on the root folder. ## Making variables ```env MYSQL_USER= MYSQL_PASSWORD= MYSQL_IP= MYSQL_PORT= MYSQL_DATABASE= ``` > [!tip] Example > my database has these variables to connect to. it doesn't mean you can copy this and make it work on yours — you have to provide your own values. > ```env > MYSQL_USER=root > MYSQL_PASSWORD= > MYSQL_IP=127.0.0.1 > MYSQL_PORT=3306 > MYSQL_DATABASE=eb_shop > ``` ## Connecting to database using the variables from [[#Making variables]] to connect to the database: ```env DATABASE_URL="mysql://${MYSQL_USER}:${MYSQL_PASSWORD}@${MYSQL_IP}:${MYSQL_PORT}/${MYSQL_DATABASE}?serverVersion=10.11.2-MariaDB&charset=utf8mb4" ``` you can copy this one if you want. drop database: ```bash symfony console doctrine:database:drop --force ``` create database: ```bash symfony console doctrine:database:create ``` # Using `compose.yaml` > [!warning] spelling > the file is named `compose.yaml` — **compose**, not **composer**. composer is the PHP package thing, easy to mix up. both files exist in a symfony project and they do totally different jobs. using `compose.yaml` is one of the great things of [[Symfony]] and docker. it allows you to create containers when needed and delete them when not used or powered off. it also allows you to migrate your project easily, because the whole setup is stored in the project itself and not inside a separate database. it's all in one file. > [!tip] IMPORTANT > change your `compose.override.yaml` to `compose.override-disabled.yaml` or basically delete it so that it doesn't interfere with your development. ## Editing `compose.yaml` everything inside this file is the same thing the manual `docker run` commands did earlier. what this basically does is create 2 containers named `webdev-mysql` and `webdev-phpmyadmin`, and their images are in the name. ```yaml services: webdev-mysql: image: mysql:8.0 container_name: webdev-mysql restart: unless-stopped environment: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD} MYSQL_DATABASE: ${MYSQL_DATABASE} MYSQL_USER: ${MYSQL_USER} MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_PASSWORD} ports: - "6666:3306" volumes: - webdev-db-data:/var/lib/mysql networks: - webdev-network webdev-phpmyadmin: image: phpmyadmin container_name: webdev-phpmyadmin restart: unless-stopped environment: PMA_HOST: webdev-mysql ports: - "7777:80" networks: - webdev-network volumes: webdev-db-data: networks: webdev-network: ``` this file is also connected to the `.env` file — that's why you see those `${MYSQL_DATABASE}` things. ## Essential commands for compose to work > [!danger] DISCLAIMER > the following commands **WILL NOT WORK** if the `terminal` you are using is **NOT** inside the root folder of your project. ### start the containers ```bash docker compose up -d ``` ### stop the containers ```bash docker compose stop ``` ### stop them and remove everything (containers + volumes) ```bash docker compose down -v ``` # How to create an entity entities are tables inside the database. (this part is still a work in progress, to be filled in properly after more discussions.) ```bash symfony console make:entity Category ``` ```bash symfony console make:migration ``` ```bash symfony console doctrine:migrations:migrate ``` ```bash symfony console make:crud Category ``` ## How to connect 2 tables when making the second entity (`Product`), the prompt asks what it is related to — these are the answers to hit: ```bash symfony console make:entity Product category <- field name ManyToOne <- the relation Category <- the other entity no <- store the whole object? yes <- is it nullable? symfony console make:migration symfony console doctrine:migrations:migrate symfony console make:crud Product ``` # See also - [[php and database]] — the mysql side these containers run - [[Symfony]] — the framework that talks to the database this sets up - [[Midterm Website]] — where all of this gets used for real

--- cssclasses: - wide tags: - notes --- # What is Docker? docker is an app that makes migrating systems, servers, databases, etc. a lot easier. the way docker does it is with **images** and **containers**. just let the next machine **install docker only**, and it's ready to migrate! # What if we don't use docker? if you don't use docker when migrating, the system might break. it could be because of: - outdated / unstable software, - no prerequisite packages, - inconsistent configuration, - and more. # Images images are one of the key features of docker. images are packages that are ready to be copied and deployed to your container so it can be used immediately. > [!note] Analogy > think of an image as a photo of a document. you can still read the document right? but you can't edit it, just scan it. > once the image has been scanned, it can then be edited again and be used again. > > in plainer terms: the image is the frozen package — you don't touch it yourself. you **run** it, and what's running it is the container. one image can spawn as many copies of a container as you want. # Containers containers are also one of the key features of docker. containers are basically tiny virtual machines with their own apps and services running — and those services would be your running images. # Setting up docker ## Images needed - mysql - php ## Create network ```bash docker network create [name of network] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > docker network create webdev-network > ``` ## most basic command to create a container > [!danger] DISCLAIMER > **NOT RECOMMENDED TO RUN THIS BY ITSELF** ```bash docker run -d [name of container] ``` > [!warning] why it's not recommended > a bare `run` like this has no network, no volume, no environment variables, nothing. the full versions below include all of those — use those instead. ## command to find if a port is used (windows) ```bash netstat -ano | findstr [portnumber] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > netstat -ano | findstr 3306 > ``` > if something is using port `3306`, you get output like this. if the port is free, the command just prints nothing. > ``` > TCP 0.0.0.0:3306 0.0.0.0:0 LISTENING 18196 > TCP [::]:3306 [::]:0 LISTENING 18196 > ``` # Creating containers this is where containers actually get created. the templates here take the full `docker run` from earlier and add the network, volume, environment variables, and port mapping you'll actually need in class. ## MySQL container ```bash docker run -d --name [ContainerName] --network [NetworkName] -v [Volume Name]:[Volume Location] -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=[Mysql Password] -e MYSQL_DATABASE=[DatabaseName] -p [host port]:[container port] [image to be installed] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > docker run -d --name webdev-mysql --network webdev-network -v webdev-db-data:/var/lib/mysql -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root -e MYSQL_DATABASE=webdev-db -p 3310:3306 mysql:8.0 > ``` ## phpMyAdmin container ```bash docker run -d --name [ContainerName] --network [NetworkName] -e PMA_HOST=[MysqlContainerName] -p [host port]:[container port] [image to be installed] ``` > [!tip] Example > ```bash > docker run -d --name webdev-phpmyadmin --network webdev-network -e PMA_HOST=webdev-mysql -p 3311:80 phpmyadmin > ``` ## My command > [!danger] DISCLAIMER > **DO NOT COPY THIS. THIS COMMAND IS IRRELEVANT TO YOUR PROJECTS** ```bash docker run -d --name EB_mysql --network EB_Network -v EB-db-data:/var/lib/mysql -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root -e MYSQL_DATABASE=EB_shop -p 6967:3306 mysql:8.0 ``` ```bash docker run -d --name EB_phpmyadmin --network EB_Network -e PMA_HOST=EB_mysql -p 6969:80 phpmyadmin ``` --- # Extra docker commands from the notes of Sir Ariel Bensing. ## Build an image from a dockerfile ```bash docker build -t symfony-app . ``` the `.` at the end matters — it points to the dockerfile in the **current folder**. ## Build the container based on the image ```bash docker run --name symfony-app-demo --network platform-network -p 8000:8000 symfony-app ``` ## Create a network ```bash docker network create platform-network ``` ## Build a container for MySQL ```bash docker run -d --name symfony-db --network platform-network -v symfony-db-data:/var/lib/mysql -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root -e MYSQL_DATABASE=app_db -p 3310:3306 mysql:8.0 ``` ## Build a container for phpMyAdmin ```bash docker run -d --name symfony-pma --network platform-network -p 8081:80 -e PMA_HOST=symfony-db phpmyadmin ``` ## Execute a command inside a running container ```bash docker exec -it symfony-app-demo "symfony command" ``` ## Inspect a network ```bash docker network inspect [network name] ``` ## Delete a network ```bash docker network rm [network name] ``` ## Delete a container ```bash docker rm [container name] ``` ## Delete an image ```bash docker rmi [image name] ``` ## Stop a container ```bash docker stop [container name] ``` took me a while to realize `stop` is for containers, not networks lmao. networks don't stop, they just exist until you `rm` them. --- # Extra on symfony to connect to your database you have to open your `.env` file on the root folder. ## Making variables ```env MYSQL_USER= MYSQL_PASSWORD= MYSQL_IP= MYSQL_PORT= MYSQL_DATABASE= ``` > [!tip] Example > my database has these variables to connect to. it doesn't mean you can copy this and make it work on yours — you have to provide your own values. > ```env > MYSQL_USER=root > MYSQL_PASSWORD= > MYSQL_IP=127.0.0.1 > MYSQL_PORT=3306 > MYSQL_DATABASE=eb_shop > ``` ## Connecting to database using the variables from [[#Making variables]] to connect to the database: ```env DATABASE_URL="mysql://${MYSQL_USER}:${MYSQL_PASSWORD}@${MYSQL_IP}:${MYSQL_PORT}/${MYSQL_DATABASE}?serverVersion=10.11.2-MariaDB&charset=utf8mb4" ``` you can copy this one if you want. drop database: ```bash symfony console doctrine:database:drop --force ``` create database: ```bash symfony console doctrine:database:create ``` # Using `compose.yaml` > [!warning] spelling > the file is named `compose.yaml` — **compose**, not **composer**. composer is the PHP package thing, easy to mix up. both files exist in a symfony project and they do totally different jobs. using `compose.yaml` is one of the great things of [[Symfony]] and docker. it allows you to create containers when needed and delete them when not used or powered off. it also allows you to migrate your project easily, because the whole setup is stored in the project itself and not inside a separate database. it's all in one file. > [!tip] IMPORTANT > change your `compose.override.yaml` to `compose.override-disabled.yaml` or basically delete it so that it doesn't interfere with your development. ## Editing `compose.yaml` everything inside this file is the same thing the manual `docker run` commands did earlier. what this basically does is create 2 containers named `webdev-mysql` and `webdev-phpmyadmin`, and their images are in the name. ```yaml services: webdev-mysql: image: mysql:8.0 container_name: webdev-mysql restart: unless-stopped environment: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD} MYSQL_DATABASE: ${MYSQL_DATABASE} MYSQL_USER: ${MYSQL_USER} MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_PASSWORD} ports: - "6666:3306" volumes: - webdev-db-data:/var/lib/mysql networks: - webdev-network webdev-phpmyadmin: image: phpmyadmin container_name: webdev-phpmyadmin restart: unless-stopped environment: PMA_HOST: webdev-mysql ports: - "7777:80" networks: - webdev-network volumes: webdev-db-data: networks: webdev-network: ``` this file is also connected to the `.env` file — that's why you see those `${MYSQL_DATABASE}` things. ## Essential commands for compose to work > [!danger] DISCLAIMER > the following commands **WILL NOT WORK** if the `terminal` you are using is **NOT** inside the root folder of your project. ### start the containers ```bash docker compose up -d ``` ### stop the containers ```bash docker compose stop ``` ### stop them and remove everything (containers + volumes) ```bash docker compose down -v ``` # How to create an entity entities are tables inside the database. (this part is still a work in progress, to be filled in properly after more discussions.) ```bash symfony console make:entity Category ``` ```bash symfony console make:migration ``` ```bash symfony console doctrine:migrations:migrate ``` ```bash symfony console make:crud Category ``` ## How to connect 2 tables when making the second entity (`Product`), the prompt asks what it is related to — these are the answers to hit: ```bash symfony console make:entity Product category <- field name ManyToOne <- the relation Category <- the other entity no <- store the whole object? yes <- is it nullable? symfony console make:migration symfony console doctrine:migrations:migrate symfony console make:crud Product ``` # See also - [[php and database]] — the mysql side these containers run - [[Symfony]] — the framework that talks to the database this sets up - [[Midterm Website]] — where all of this gets used for real

Making variables ```env MYSQL_USER= MYSQL_PASSWORD= MYSQL_IP= MYSQL_PORT= MYSQL_DATABASE= ``` > [!tip] Example > my database has these variables to connect to. it doesn't mean you can copy this and make it work on yours — you have to provide your own values. > ```env > MYSQL_USER=root > MYSQL_PASSWORD= > MYSQL_IP=127.0.0.1 > MYSQL_PORT=3306 > MYSQL_DATABASE=eb_shop > ``` ## Connecting to database using the variables from [[#Making variables]] to connect to the database: ```env DATABASE_URL="mysql://${MYSQL_USER}:${MYSQL_PASSWORD}@${MYSQL_IP}:${MYSQL_PORT}/${MYSQL_DATABASE}?serverVersion=10.11.2-MariaDB&charset=utf8mb4" ``` you can copy this one if you want. drop database: ```bash symfony console doctrine:database:drop --force ``` create database: ```bash symfony console doctrine:database:create ``` # Using `compose.yaml` > [!warning] spelling > the file is named `compose.yaml` — **compose**, not **composer**. composer is the PHP package thing, easy to mix up. both files exist in a symfony project and they do totally different jobs. using `compose.yaml` is one of the great things of [[Symfony]] and docker. it allows you to create containers when needed and delete them when not used or powered off. it also allows you to migrate your project easily, because the whole setup is stored in the project itself and not inside a separate database. it's all in one file. > [!tip] IMPORTANT > change your `compose.override.yaml` to `compose.override-disabled.yaml` or basically delete it so that it doesn't interfere with your development. ## Editing `compose.yaml` everything inside this file is the same thing the manual `docker run` commands did earlier. what this basically does is create 2 containers named `webdev-mysql` and `webdev-phpmyadmin`, and their images are in the name. ```yaml services: webdev-mysql: image: mysql:8.0 container_name: webdev-mysql restart: unless-stopped environment: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD} MYSQL_DATABASE: ${MYSQL_DATABASE} MYSQL_USER: ${MYSQL_USER} MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_PASSWORD} ports: - "6666:3306" volumes: - webdev-db-data:/var/lib/mysql networks: - webdev-network webdev-phpmyadmin: image: phpmyadmin container_name: webdev-phpmyadmin restart: unless-stopped environment: PMA_HOST: webdev-mysql ports: - "7777:80" networks: - webdev-network volumes: webdev-db-data: networks: webdev-network: ``` this file is also connected to the `.env` file — that's why you see those `${MYSQL_DATABASE}` things. ## Essential commands for compose to work > [!danger] DISCLAIMER > the following commands **WILL NOT WORK** if the `terminal` you are using is **NOT** inside the root folder of the project. > [!note] see original > for the exact compose command list, check [[Docker]] — this part of the original note wasn't fully captured when this note was made. # See also - [[Symfony]] — the framework the containers run on the original note - [[Docker]] — the original standalone note - [[php and database]] — the vanilla connect-and-save this framework replaces - [[Midterm Website]] — where symfony is used for the admin panel
